title: Chapter 3 : Cellular Basis Of Life
content:

የመጀመሪያውን ክፍል (Part 1) በደንብ አድርጋችሁ እንዳነበባችሁት ሙሉ እምነት አለን! 🌟 አሁን ደግሞ የPart 1 የቀጠለውንና በፈተና ላይ እጅግ ከፍተኛ ነጥብ የሚያስይዘውን Chapter 3 (Part 2): Mitochondria, Chloroplasts, Cytoskeleton & Plasma Membrane የፈተና ዝግጅት ኖት ይዘንላችሁ ቀርበናል። በጥሞና ተከታተሉን!👇👇👇

📝 Self Test Questions & Detailed Solutions

1. Explain why mitochondria are considered unusual organelles compared to others:
Mitochondria are unusual in two main ways: (a) They contain their own unique circular DNA in their matrix, known as mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), and (b) They possess the ability to replicate themselves independently, even when the host cell is not undergoing cell division.

2. Describe the Fluid Mosaic Model of the plasma membrane and the role of cholesterol:
The plasma membrane consists of a fluid phospholipid bilayer embedded with proteins floating in an ever-changing 'mosaic' pattern. Phospholipids have polar charged hydrophilic heads facing outward toward ECF/ICF and non-polar hydrophobic fatty acid tails facing inward. Cholesterol sits between phospholipid molecules to provide both fluidity and stability, preventing fatty acid chains from packing together and crystallizing, acting like a plug to reduce polar molecule leakage while giving the cell flexibility to change shape.

3. Differentiate between Microtubules and Microfilaments in structure and function:
Microtubules are the largest cytoskeletal elements composed of hollow tubes of globular tubulin protein (6 nm unit diameter); they maintain asymmetrical cell shape (e.g., long axon in neurons), transport vesicles, power cilia/flagella, and distribute chromosomes during cell division. Microfilaments are the smallest cytoskeletal elements composed of the protein actin; they function as a cellular contractile system and mechanical stiffeners.

3.3. Structure and Function of Organelles (Continued)

7. Mitochondria ("Powerhouses of the Cell")

Mitochondria are the "power houses" of a cell; they extract energy from nutrients in food and transform it into a usable chemical energy form (ATP) to energize cellular activities. Their number varies from a few hundreds to thousands depending on the metabolic energy needs of the specific cell type (e.g., a single liver cell contains ~800 mitochondria).

Structural Features of Mitochondria:

  • Shape & Size: Rod or oval-shaped, roughly the size of a bacterium (0.5 µm wide up to 10 µm long).
  • Double Membrane System:
    • Outer Membrane: Smooth outer membrane that surrounds the organelle.
    • Inner Membrane: Infolded into a series of enfoldings or shelves called cristae, which project into the inner cavity. Cristae contain electron transport chain proteins that convert energy into a usable form during oxidative phosphorylation, greatly expanding surface area for energy production.
  • Matrix: The inner cavity filled with a jelly-like fluid containing a mixture of hundreds of dissolved enzymes (Citric Acid / TCA Cycle enzymes) essential for extracting energy, as well as RNA and unique mitochondrial DNA.

Energy Transformation Mechanism (ATP Dynamics):

  • Carbon-hydrogen bonds in ingested food store chemical energy.
  • Body cells extract this energy and convert it into high-energy phosphate bonds of ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) — the universal energy carrier and common energy "currency" of the body ("cash in" ATP to pay the energy "price" of cellular work).
  • Splitting the terminal high-energy phosphate bond yields immediate usable energy:
    ATP ➔ ADP + Inorganic Phosphate (Pᵢ) + Energy

Unusual Features of Mitochondria:

  1. Matrix DNA: Possess their own unique circular DNA called mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) located in the matrix.
  2. Self-Replication: Capable of replicating themselves independently, even when the host cell to which they belong is not undergoing cell division.

👉 Mitochondria የሴሏ Powerhouse (የኃይል ማመንጫ) ነው! ከምግብ የምናገኘውን ጉልበት ወደ ሴሏ ሳንቲም ወይም Currency ወደሆነው ATP ይለውጣል። ATP ሲሰበር energy + ADP + Pi ይሰጠናል። Mitochondria ሁለት ልዩ ነገሮች አሉት፡ 1) በውስጡ Matrix የሚባል ፈሳሽና የራሱ mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) አለው፤ 2) ሴሏ ሳትከፈል እንኳን እራሱን የማባዛት (Self-replicate) ልዩ ችሎታ አለው!

💡 Exam Hint:
1. 'Which organelle contains its own unique DNA and can replicate independently of host cell division?' -> Mitochondria.
2. 'TCA / Citric Acid cycle enzymes are located in which part of the mitochondrion?' -> Matrix.
3. 'Where are electron transport chain proteins located?' -> Cristae (Inner Membrane).

😅 EthioFresh Humor Break:
Mitochondria የራሱ DNA ያለውና የራሱን ውሳኔ የሚወስን ገለልተኛ ኦርጋኔል ነው! እናንተም በፈተና ወቅት እንደ Mitochondria በራሳችሁ በራስ መተማመን ተዘጋጁ! 😅

8. Chloroplasts

Found in plant cells and plastids, chloroplasts conduct photosynthesis — a process by which plants synthesize their own food by converting light energy into stored chemical energy. They are located on the outer surface of plant cells to receive sufficient light and appear green due to the presence of chlorophyll pigments in their internal parts.

9. Vesicles and Vacuoles

  • Vesicles: Small, membrane-bound sacs used to store or transport substances around the cell. (Lysosomes are actually specialized vesicles).
  • Vacuoles: Essentially larger vesicles formed by the joining together of many vesicles. They are membrane-bound organelles with no specific shape that contain water with a number of different compounds within it. In plant cells, vacuoles are critical for maintaining Turgor Pressure (structural stiffness).

10. Cytoskeleton ("Bone and Muscle" of the Cell)

The cytoskeleton is a complex protein network acting as the internal "bone and muscle" of the cell. This necessary intracellular scaffolding supports and organizes cellular components, controls their movements, and provides distinct shape and size to the cell.

Four Main Cytoskeletal Elements:

ElementProtein Unit & Structural FeaturesKey Roles & Functions
MicrotubulesLargest of the group; slender, long, hollow tubes composed of globular tubulin protein (6 nm unit diameter).• Provide asymmetrical cell shape (e.g., neuron with cell body and long axon).
• Coordinate transport of secretory vesicles.
• Power movements of cilia and flagella.
• Distribute chromosomes during cell division.
MicrofilamentsSmallest of the cytoskeleton; composed of globular protein actin (similar shape to tubulin).• Cellular contractile system.
• Serve as mechanical stiffeners.
Intermediate FilamentsTough, insoluble protein fibers.• Provide mechanical support and resist tensile stress.
Microtubular LatticeInterconnected protein meshwork.• Suspends organelles within the cytosol.

Summary Functions Provided / Determined by Cytoskeleton:

  1. Determines and maintains the shape of a cell.
  2. Provides structural support.
  3. Organizes internal cell contents.
  4. Facilitates substance movement through cell (cilia, flagella, and intracytoplasmic vesicles).
  5. Contributes to movements of the cell as a whole.

👉 Cytoskeleton የሴሏ Bone and Muscle (አጥንትና ጡንቻ) ነው። 4 ክፍሎች አሉት፡ Microtubules (ትልልቆቹ - ከ Tubulin የተሰሩ፤ የሴል ቅርፅ ይይዛሉ፣ ክሮሞዞምን በሴል ክፍፍል ወቅት ይከፍላሉ)፤ Microfilaments (ትንንሾቹ - ከ Actin የተሰሩ፤ ለሴል ኮንትራክሽን ያገለግላሉ)፤ Intermediate Filaments እና Microtubular lattice። Vacuole በዕፅዋት ውስጥ Turgor Pressure ይጠብቃል።

💡 Exam Hint:
1. 'Which cytoskeletal structure is made of tubulin and moves chromosomes during cell division?' -> Microtubules.
2. 'Which organelle maintains turgor pressure in plant cells?' -> Vacuole.

3.4. Plasma / Cell Membrane Structure & The Fluid Mosaic Model

The plasma membrane is an extremely thin layer of lipids and proteins forming the outermost boundary of a living cell, enclosing the Intracellular Fluid (ICF) and separating it from the Extracellular Fluid (ECF) environment. It serves as a mechanical barrier that traps needed molecules within the cell and plays an active role in selective permeability. Under electron microscopy, it appears as a 'trilaminar' layer structure having two dark outer layers separated by a light middle layer.

Chemical Composition of the Plasma Membrane:

1. Lipid Bilayer (Phospholipids & Cholesterol)

The lipid bilayer forms the basic structure of the membrane and is fluid in nature, with a consistency like liquid cooking oil. It acts as a primary barrier to the passage of water-soluble substances between ICF and ECF.

  • Phospholipids: Most abundant membrane lipids. Possess a two-sided (amphipathic) structure:
    • Polar Head: Negatively charged phosphate group; hydrophilic ("water-loving"); faces outward in contact with ECF and inward in contact with ICF.
    • Two Non-Polar Tails: Electrically neutral fatty acid chains; hydrophobic ("water-fearing"); bury themselves in the center away from water to form the internal core.
  • Cholesterol: Tucked between the phosphate molecules and fatty acid chains. Functions:
    • Provides both fluidity and stability.
    • Prevents fatty acid chains from packing together and crystallizing (which would decrease membrane fluidity).
    • Acts like a plug, reducing even further the escape or entry of polar molecules through the membrane.
    • Exerts a regulatory role on membrane proteins and gives flexibility for cell shape changes.

2. Membrane Proteins & Their Specialized Roles

Membrane proteins are attached to or inserted within the lipid bilayer (some spanning the entire thickness, others anchored on inner/outer surfaces). Many float freely, creating an ever-changing 'mosaic pattern'. They perform most specific membrane functions:

Protein TypeStructure & Specific Functional Mechanism
1. ChannelsWater-filled passage ways across the bilayer; selectively allow specific small ions (Na+, K+, Ca2+, Cl-) to pass without touching the lipid interior. Selectivity is determined by charged amino acid groups. Channels open and close via gating mechanisms.
2. Carrier ProteinsBind and transport specific molecules that cannot cross on their own (e.g., thyroid epithelial cells possess carriers for iodine).
3. ReceptorsSpecific binding sites on the outer surface that recognize and bind chemical messengers (hormones in blood, neurotransmitters in nerve cells), triggering intracellular signaling events.
4. Membrane-Bound EnzymesControl specific chemical reactions on either side of the membrane (e.g., ACh-esterase on skeletal muscle membranes destroys acetylcholine to stop contraction; digestive enzymes on microvilli lining the gut).
5. Structural AnchorsArranged as filament networks/meshworks on the inner side secured to internal cytoskeletal proteins to maintain cell shape.
6. Cell Adhesion Molecules (CAMs)Protrude from the membrane surface to grip adjacent cells or connective tissue fibers interlacing between cells. Some have carbohydrates on their outermost tip.
7. Cell-Identity Markers (Antigens)Glycoproteins with branching carbohydrate side chains acting like "antennae" / "name tags" for self-recognition, tissue organization, and immune system detection of foreign invaders.

3. Membrane Carbohydrates & Surface Asymmetry

  • Asymmetry: The plasma membrane is strictly asymmetrical — the inner and outer halves are not the same. Short-chain carbohydrates exist only on the outer surface, and protein/lipid compositions differ between inner and outer surfaces.
  • Glycoproteins & Glycolipids: Short-chain carbohydrates bound primarily to membrane proteins (glycoproteins) and to a lesser extent to lipids (glycolipids).
  • Functions of Surface Carbohydrates & Glycolipids:
    1. Self-Recognition ("Trademark"): Allows cells to recognize each other and organize into tissues and organs.
    2. Growth Inhibition: Surface markers contact neighboring cells to prevent overgrowth (abnormal markers on tumor cells cause uncontrolled growth).
    3. Receptor & Cell Binding: Glycolipids act as receptor sites for chemical signals and work with glycoproteins to stick correct cells together in tissues (e.g., sperm recognition of egg cells / ova).

4. Energy Transfer in Membranes

Proteins embedded within biological membranes also take part in energy transfer systems: proteins in the internal membranes of chloroplasts drive photosynthetic energy capture, while proteins in mitochondrial cristae drive cellular respiration and ATP synthesis.

👉 Plasma membrane በ Fluid Mosaic Model ይገለፃል:: Phospholipids ውሃ የሚወድ ራስ (Hydrophilic head) እና ውሃ የሚፈራ ጭራ (Hydrophobic tail) አላቸው:: Cholesterol በፋቲ አሲዶች መካከል በመግባት ሜምብሬኑ እንዳይረጋና እንዳይፈርስ Fluidity እና Stability ይሰጣል:: ፕሮቲኖች 7 ዋና ስራ አላቸው፡ Channels (አዮን ማለፊያ)፣ Carriers (ትልልቅ ሞለኪውል ማጓጓዣ)፣ Receptors (ሆርሞን መቀበያ)፣ Enzymes (ኢንዛይም - ለምሳሌ ACh-esterase)፣ Cytoskeleton Anchors (ቅርፅ ጠባቂ)፣ CAMs (ሴሎችን የሚያያይዙ)፣ እና Cell-identity markers (መታወቂያ):: Carbohydrate የሚገኘው በውጭ በኩል ብቻ (Asymmetrical) ሲሆን የሴሏ መታወቂያ ሆኖ ያገለግላል።

💡 Exam Hint:
1. 'What is the function of cholesterol in the plasma membrane?' -> Prevents fatty acid chains from packing together and crystallizing, maintaining fluidity, stability, and acting as a plug against polar molecule loss.
2. 'Which enzyme on skeletal muscle membranes breaks down neurotransmitters?' -> Acetylcholinesterase (ACh-esterase).
3. 'Why is the plasma membrane termed asymmetrical?' -> Carbohydrates are present ONLY on the outer surface, and protein/lipid compositions differ between inner and outer layers.

😅 EthioFresh Humor Break:
Cholesterol በሴል ሜምብሬን ውስጥ 'Fluidity' እና 'Stability' እንደሚጠብቅ ሁሉ፣ እናንተም በዩኒቨርሲቲ ህይወታችሁ የጥናትና የእረፍት ጊዜያችሁን ሚዛን ጠብቁ! 😅
